title: shutdown
summary: Ask running lsp engines to close their indexes and stand down, so an index can be rebuilt without killing them
intro: Read this when you need to rebuild an index that running engines hold open: shutdown asks the running lsp engines to close their stores and stand down, without killing them.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint shutdown [--db <file.sqlite>]... [--wait <sec>] [--dry-run] [--all] [--force] (ask running `lsp` engines to stand down: close every store, exit 0)
help: drag-lint shutdown [--db <file.sqlite>]... [--wait <sec>] [--dry-run] [--all] [--force]   (ask running `lsp` engines to stand down: close every store, exit 0)
transport: a Windows NAMED PIPE, never a TCP port -- \\.\pipe\drag-lint-ctl-<sid>-s<session>-p<pid>, created with an
explicit DACL for the creating user only, so another user or session cannot signal your engines. Only an
engine started in lsp mode listens (one-shot verbs and `serve` do not). --all (the default) asks every
reachable engine; --db keeps only engines holding that index; --dry-run lists them and changes nothing.
--wait (default 5 s) bounds the graceful wait per engine: one inside a request answers BUSY and keeps
running (exit 1). --force TerminateProcess'es ONLY an engine that refused or did not answer, and says
